newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAPAN CONSTRUCTION COS DROOP AS SELLERS CUT LOSSES.
newsitem.headline: JAPAN CONSTRUCTION COS DROOP AS SELLERS CUT LOSSES.

text.p: Japanese builder stocks drooped in the Thursday afternoon session, some hitting record lows, as investors stepped up sales in the sector in order to cut their losses, traders said.

They said that while there were no new developments which prompted the selling, investors were discouraged that the construction share prices were showing no signs of recovery. Many issues were now under 100 yen per share.

As of 0509 GMT, Fujita Corp shares were down 21 yen or 18.10 percent at 95 yen, a new record low making it the largest percentage loser on the first section of the Tokyo bourse. With trade totalling 5.79 million shares, it was the second most heavily traded issue.
Aoki Corp had lost six yen to reach 61.
Shokusan Jutaku Sogo Co Ltd was down eight yen at 79.
"Until the middle of the morning session, Fujita shares were around 110 yen," a trader at a second-tier brokerage said.
"There doesn't seem to be any news to hurt the shares, but after it slipped below the 100 yen line in the afternoon, the selling has snowballed," he added.
